Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Time, the calendar & feasts

generation noun

people born at about the same time; the span of a lifetime

also generations, my generation, the younger generation, future generations, for generations, three generations

classical

Cic. Sen. 31: tertiam jam enim aetātem hominum vidēbat
Hor. Carm. 3.6.46: aetās parentum, pejor avīs

aetās, aetātis f.

noun, third declension

a generation; an age, a time

Lewis & Short: a space of time, an age, generation; nostrā aetāte, in our time (Quint. 1.4.20).

Other words

  • saeculum, saeculī n. — a generation of people; a lifetime, an age

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 24 (Caecilius): serit arborēs quae alterī saeclō prōsint; Cic. Amic. 15: ex omnibus saeculīs

    Lewis & Short: the human race living in a particular age, a generation, the times; also a century (see century). Saeclum is the shortened form of old Latin and of poetry.

  • aequālēs, aequālium m. pl. — people of one’s own age: one’s generation

    noun, third declension, plural: the adjective aequālis used as a noun · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 101: cum aequālibus; Plaut. Trin. 48: Ō amīce, salvē, atque aequālis

    One’s contemporaries, those born about when one was.

  • posterī, posterōrum m. pl. — future generations, posterity

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 25: posterīs prōdere

    Lewis & Short: coming generations, descendants, posterity.

  • generātiō, generātiōnis f. — a generation of people

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Eph. 3.5 (Lewis & Short); Ambr. Off. 1.25.121 (Lewis & Short)

    Christian Latin, after the Greek of the Gospels; classically a begetting (Pliny).

Examples

  • serit arborēs quae alterī saeclō prōsint

    he plants trees to be of use to the next generationCic. Sen. 24 (Caecilius)

  • aetās parentum, pejor avīs, tulit nōs nēquiōrēs, mox datūrōs prōgeniem vitiōsiōrem

    our parents’ generation, worse than our grandparents’, bore us, worse still, and we shall soon have children more wicked yetHor. Carm. 3.6.46–48

  • Tertiam jam enim aetātem hominum vidēbat

    for he was already seeing a third generation of menCic. Sen. 31

See also century, parents, older, year.
